scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4659: Several users report intermittent slowness and claim
"router0 is dropping our packets" -- they think router0 is silently discarding
traffic it should forward (a forwarding/ACL problem or an overloaded box) and want
it restarted. Please confirm that router0 is dropping traffic and tell us the fix.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 has ip_forward enabled, its interfaces
  are up, and traffic transiting router0 between segments arrives with 0% loss; there
  is no drop-inducing ACL or forwarding fault. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of packet loss on router0 that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- router0 dropping/forwarding
traffic incorrectly -- is NOT reproducible: a ping across router0 (between two
segments it connects) completes with 0% loss, router0 has ip_forward enabled, its
interfaces are up, ripd is running, and there is no drop-inducing ACL.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: router0 is forwarding correctly and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces a path transiting
router0, finds 0% loss, checks router0's ip_forward, interfaces, and any filters, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" router0 dropping packets -- blaming an ACL,
forwarding, or load to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk ticket's premise is incorrect — router0 is not dropping, throttling, or
silently discarding any traffic. A comprehensive inspection of every relevant
forwarding subsystem on router0 found no anomaly whatsoever.

Specifically: (1) iptables on router0 has completely empty INPUT, FORWARD, and OUTPUT
chains with an ACCEPT default policy — there are no ACLs or firewall rules that
could silently drop forwarded traffic. (2) The TC queueing discipline on all three
of router0's interfaces (eth0/eth1/eth2) is the default kernel fq_codel with no
custom shaper, policer, or rate limiter attached. (3) IP forwarding is enabled
(ip_forward=1). (4) The kernel interface counters show exactly zero RX-dropped and
zero TX-dropped frames on eth0, eth1, and eth2. (5) The conntrack statistics table
shows zero drops across all CPUs. (6) RIP is stable: all eight prefixes are present
in router0's table with correct next-hops and metrics, the peer 10.10.0.2 (router1)
has zero bad-packet and bad-route counts, and routes were refreshed seconds ago.
(7) End-to-end pings across every segment through router0 — IT-LAN to servers,
CS-LAN to office, principle-LAN to servers — all complete with 0% packet loss.

Root cause: There is no network fault. The perceived "slowness" was not caused by
router0 dropping packets; no injected fault or misconfiguration is present anywhere
in the topology. Restarting router0 would be unnecessary and disruptive.

Corrective fix: No fix is required. Close the ticket as a false alarm and investigate
the end-host applications or user-side conditions (e.g., local Wi-Fi, application
timeouts) that gave rise to the perception of packet loss.
